message.content: <local-command-caveat>Caveat: The messages below were generated by the user while running local commands. DO NOT respond to these messages or otherwise consider them in your response unless the user explicitly asks you to.</local-command-caveat>
<local-command-stdout>Set effort level to ultracode (this session only): xhigh + dynamic workflow orchestration</local-command-stdout>

You are the FRONT-END track for Labmate, an agent-native data science harness.
You build the mission-control cockpit in a NEW directory apps/cockpit (do not
edit apps/web — that's the back-end track). Your contract is
apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml; build entirely against the Prism mock at
http://localhost:4010 using the generated types in packages/api-types.

Read first:
  - apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml   (every shape you render comes from here)
  - docs/BRIEF.md (section 9, the cockpit)  and docs/DEMO_SCRIPT.md
  - packages/api-types/index.ts  (generated TS types — import these, do not hand-write shapes)

The cockpit is a four-pane mission control, NOT a dashboard:
  1. Brief + rubric — objective, metric, guardrails, budget, "done" criteria.
  2. Experiment cards — per hypothesis: statement, expected impact, cost,
     status, latest metric, agent rationale, and approve / deny / rerun buttons.
  3. Evidence ledger — timeline of runs, notes, critiques, human feedback.
  4. Current recommendation — e.g. "Promote model 7 after a calibration check."
Plus a natural-language feedback box that POSTs to /api/feedback, and a
"Generate report" button that POSTs to /api/reports and links the artifact.

Rules of engagement:
  1. The spec is the source of truth. If you need a field it lacks, STOP and
     propose a spec edit — do not invent response shapes or hardcode mock data
     beyond what the spec describes.
  2. Read everything from GET /api/studies and GET /api/studies/{id}. All writes
     go to the documented POST routes with the bearer token from an env var.
  3. Make it resilient: loading and empty states for every pane, optimistic UI
     on approve/deny, and graceful handling of a run still "running".
  4. Use VITE_API_BASE so flipping from the mock (:4010) to the real Worker
     (:8787 / the deployed URL) is a one-line change. /goal Build the Labmate cockpit in apps/cockpit against the Prism mock at
VITE_API_BASE. Done means: a study-list view (GET /api/studies) and a study
detail view rendering all four panes from GET /api/studies/{studyId}; experiment
cards with working approve/deny/rerun that POST to /api/feedback and
/api/approvals/request; a natural-language feedback box; a run table fed by the
study detail's runs with status, metrics, and linked critiques; a "Generate
report" button hitting /api/reports that surfaces the artifact link; every pane
has loading and empty states; the app imports types from packages/api-types and
builds with `npm run build` clean; and switching VITE_API_BASE to the wrangler
URL renders real data with no code change.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- agents-sdk: Build AI agents on Cloudflare Workers using the Agents SDK. Load when creating stateful agents, durable workflows, real-time WebSocket apps, scheduled tasks, MCP servers, chat applications, voice agents, or browser automation. Covers Agent class, state management, callable RPC, Workflows, durable execution, queues, retries, observability, and React hooks. Biases towards retrieval from Cloudflare docs over pre-trained knowledge.
- cloudflare: Comprehensive Cloudflare platform skill covering Workers, Pages, storage (KV, D1, R2), AI (Workers AI, Vectorize, Agents SDK), feature flags (Flagship), networking (Tunnel, Spectrum), security (WAF, DDoS), and infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Pulumi). Use for any Cloudflare development task. Biases towards retrieval from Cloudflare docs over pre-trained knowledge.
- cloudflare-email-service: Send and receive transactional emails with Cloudflare Email Service (Email Sending + Email Routing). Use when building email sending (Workers binding or REST API), email routing, Agents SDK email handling, or integrating email into any app — Workers, Node.js, Python, Go, etc. Also use for email deliverability, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, wrangler email setup, MCP email tools, or when a coding agent needs to send emails. Even for simple requests like "add email to my Worker" — this skill has critical config details.
- durable-objects: Create and review Cloudflare Durable Objects. Use when building stateful coordination (chat rooms, multiplayer games, booking systems), implementing RPC methods, SQLite storage, alarms, WebSockets, or reviewing DO code for best practices. Covers Workers integration, wrangler config, and testing with Vitest. Biases towards retrieval from Cloudflare docs over pre-trained knowledge.
- sandbox-sdk: Build sandboxed applications for secure code execution. Load when building AI code execution, code interpreters, CI/CD systems, interactive dev environments, or executing untrusted code. Covers Sandbox SDK lifecycle, commands, files, code interpreter, and preview URLs. Biases towards retrieval from Cloudflare docs over pre-trained knowledge.
- steel-browser: Use this skill for any web task where WebFetch or curl would fail or be insufficient — pages that require JavaScript to render, forms to fill and submit, screenshots or PDFs of live pages, CAPTCHA/bot-protection bypass, login flows, and multi-step browser navigation with persistent session state. WebFetch returns empty HTML for JS-rendered pages; this skill runs a real cloud browser that executes JavaScript, maintains cookies, clicks buttons, and handles anti-bot measures. Trigger when the user wants you to actually perform a web task (visit, interact, extract, capture) rather than just write code for it. Skip only for: static pages a simple GET can fetch, localhost or private-network targets, writing browser automation code the user will run themselves, or conceptual questions about browser tools.
- turnstile-spin: Set up Cloudflare Turnstile end-to-end in a project — scan the codebase, create the widget via the Cloudflare API, deploy the managed siteverify Worker, write the frontend snippets, validate, and persist the skill. Load this when a user asks to add Turnstile, set up CAPTCHA, protect a form from bots, or fix a Turnstile integration. Mirrors developers.cloudflare.com/turnstile/spin.
- web-perf: Analyzes web performance using Chrome DevTools MCP. Measures Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS) and supplementary metrics (FCP, TBT, Speed Index), identifies render-blocking resources, network dependency chains, layout shifts, caching issues, and accessibility gaps. Use when asked to audit, profile, debug, or optimize page load performance, Lighthouse scores, or site speed. Biases towards retrieval from current documentation over pre-trained knowledge.
- workers-best-practices: Reviews and authors Cloudflare Workers code against production best practices. Load when writing new Workers, reviewing Worker code, configuring wrangler.jsonc, or checking for common Workers anti-patterns (streaming, floating promises, global state, secrets, bindings, observability). Biases towards retrieval from Cloudflare docs over pre-trained knowledge.
- wrangler: Cloudflare Workers CLI for deploying, developing, and managing Workers, KV, R2, D1, Vectorize, Hyperdrive, Workers AI, Containers, Queues, Workflows, Pipelines, and Secrets Store. Load before running wrangler commands to ensure correct syntax and best practices. Biases towards retrieval from Cloudflare docs over pre-trained knowledge.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Create distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces with high design quality. Use this skill when the user asks to build web components, pages, or applications. Generates creative, polished code that avoids generic AI aesthetics.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.content:
1	openapi: 3.1.0
2	info:
3	  title: Labmate Control Plane API
4	  version: 0.1.0
5	  description: >
6	    The Labmate control plane is the Cloudflare Worker (apps/web) that the MCP
7	    server and the cockpit both talk to. It is the single contract for parallel
8	    front-end / back-end work: the back end implements these routes against D1,
9	    R2, and the Durable Object; the front end builds the cockpit against a mock
10	    generated from this file. Neither side has to wait for the other.
11	
12	    Conventions
13	    -----------
14	    * All write routes mirror a semantic MCP tool (create_study, profile_dataset,
15	      propose_experiments, request_approval, launch_experiment, query_runs,
16	      record_human_feedback, write_report, grade_study_against_rubric).
17	    * Writes require the shared internal bearer token (LABMATE_INTERNAL_TOKEN).
18	      Reads used by the cockpit are public.
19	    * Entity shapes mirror packages/schemas/*.schema.json and apps/web/schema.sql.
20	      If you change an entity, change it there and here together.
21	    * The evidence ledger is the product: every run links to a hypothesis and
22	      carries rationale; every critique and decision is recorded.
23	
24	servers:
25	  - url: http://localhost:8787
26	    description: Local wrangler dev
27	  - url: https://labmate.{your-subdomain}.workers.dev
28	    description: Deployed Worker (this becomes LABMATE_PUBLIC_URL)
29	    variables:
30	      your-subdomain:
31	        default: example
32	
33	tags:
34	  - name: studies
35	    description: Create studies and read the full evidence ledger.
36	  - name: experiments
37	    description: Propose hypotheses and launch sandboxed runs.
38	  - name: approvals
39	    description: Human approval gates for compute and risky actions.
40	  - name: feedback
41	    description: Human business judgment, parsed into experiment constraints.
42	  - name: reports
43	    description: Reproducible model cards with provenance.
44	  - name: grading
45	    description: Machine-gradable definition of done.
46	
47	security:
48	  - internalToken: []
49	
50	paths:
51	  /api/studies:
52	    post:
53	      tags: [studies]
54	      operationId: createStudy
55	      summary: Create a study (create_study)
56	      description: >
57	        Opens the evidence ledger from a brief. The human supplies business
58	        judgment (objective, target, metric, constraints, budget); this returns
59	        the study id everything else hangs off.
60	      security:
61	        - internalToken: []
62	      requestBody:
63	        required: true
64	        content:
65	          application/json:
66	            schema:
67	              $ref: "#/components/schemas/CreateStudyRequest"
68	            examples:
69	              slaTickets:
70	                $ref: "#/components/examples/CreateStudySlaTickets"
71	      responses:
72	        "201":
73	          description: Study created.
74	          content:
75	            application/json:
76	              schema:
77	                $ref: "#/components/schemas/CreateStudyResponse"
78	        "400": { $ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest" }
79	        "401": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized" }
80	    get:
81	      tags: [studies]
82	      operationId: listStudies
83	      summary: List studies (cockpit home)
84	      description: Read route the cockpit uses to render the study list. Public.
85	      security: []
86	      parameters:
87	        - name: status
88	          in: query
89	          required: false
90	          schema:
91	            type: string
92	            enum: [open, done, stopped]
93	        - name: limit
94	          in: query
95	          required: false
96	          schema: { type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 100, default: 20 }
97	      responses:
98	        "200":
99	          description: A list of studies.
100	          content:
101	            application/json:
102	              schema:
103	                type: object
104	                required: [studies]
105	                properties:
106	                  studies:
107	                    type: array
108	                    items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Study" }
109	
110	  /api/studies/{studyId}:
111	    parameters:
112	      - $ref: "#/components/parameters/StudyId"
113	    get:
114	      tags: [studies]
115	      operationId: getStudy
116	      summary: Full study detail / evidence ledger (study detail)
117	      description: >
118	        The cockpit's main read and the shape grade_study.py fetches. Returns the
119	        study plus its dataset version, hypotheses, runs, critiques, decisions,
120	        feedback, and artifacts — the whole ledger in one call. Public.
121	      security: []
122	      responses:
123	        "200":
124	          description: The study and its complete ledger.
125	          content:
126	            application/json:
127	              schema:
128	                $ref: "#/components/schemas/StudyDetail"
129	        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
130	
131	  /api/profile:
132	    post:
133	      tags: [studies]
134	      operationId: profileDataset
135	      summary: Profile the dataset (profile_dataset)
136	      description: >
137	        Profiles the study's dataset and writes a dataset version: columns with
138	        dtypes and missingness, candidate leakage columns (flagged, defaulting to
139	        banned), the split strategy, and the seed.
140	      security:
141	        - internalToken: []
142	      requestBody:
143	        required: true
144	        content:
145	          application/json:
146	            schema:
147	              type: object
148	              required: [study_id]
149	              properties:
150	                study_id: { type: string }
151	      responses:
152	        "200":
153	          description: Dataset profiled; data contract written.
154	          content:
155	            application/json:
156	              schema:
157	                $ref: "#/components/schemas/DatasetVersion"
158	        "401": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized" }
159	        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
160	
161	  /api/experiments/propose:
162	    post:
163	      tags: [experiments]
164	      operationId: proposeExperiments
165	      summary: Propose hypothesis cards (propose_experiments)
166	      description: >
167	        Returns N hypothesis cards (statement, rationale, model family, candidate
168	        features, expected outcome). These render as the experiment cards in the
169	        cockpit; the human approves, edits, or rejects them.
170	      security:
171	        - internalToken: []
172	      requestBody:
173	        required: true
174	        content:
175	          application/json:
176	            schema:
177	              type: object
178	              required: [study_id]
179	              properties:
180	                study_id: { type: string }

file.content:
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Labmate Control Plane API
  version: 0.1.0
  description: >
    The Labmate control plane is the Cloudflare Worker (apps/web) that the MCP
    server and the cockpit both talk to. It is the single contract for parallel
    front-end / back-end work: the back end implements these routes against D1,
    R2, and the Durable Object; the front end builds the cockpit against a mock
    generated from this file. Neither side has to wait for the other.

    Conventions
    -----------
    * All write routes mirror a semantic MCP tool (create_study, profile_dataset,
      propose_experiments, request_approval, launch_experiment, query_runs,
      record_human_feedback, write_report, grade_study_against_rubric).
    * Writes require the shared internal bearer token (LABMATE_INTERNAL_TOKEN).
      Reads used by the cockpit are public.
    * Entity shapes mirror packages/schemas/*.schema.json and apps/web/schema.sql.
      If you change an entity, change it there and here together.
    * The evidence ledger is the product: every run links to a hypothesis and
      carries rationale; every critique and decision is recorded.

servers:
  - url: http://localhost:8787
    description: Local wrangler dev
  - url: https://labmate.{your-subdomain}.workers.dev
    description: Deployed Worker (this becomes LABMATE_PUBLIC_URL)
    variables:
      your-subdomain:
        default: example

tags:
  - name: studies
    description: Create studies and read the full evidence ledger.
  - name: experiments
    description: Propose hypotheses and launch sandboxed runs.
  - name: approvals
    description: Human approval gates for compute and risky actions.
  - name: feedback
    description: Human business judgment, parsed into experiment constraints.
  - name: reports
    description: Reproducible model cards with provenance.
  - name: grading
    description: Machine-gradable definition of done.

security:
  - internalToken: []

paths:
  /api/studies:
    post:
      tags: [studies]
      operationId: createStudy
      summary: Create a study (create_study)
      description: >
        Opens the evidence ledger from a brief. The human supplies business
        judgment (objective, target, metric, constraints, budget); this returns
        the study id everything else hangs off.
      security:
        - internalToken: []
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: "#/components/schemas/CreateStudyRequest"
            examples:
              slaTickets:
                $ref: "#/components/examples/CreateStudySlaTickets"
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Study created.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/CreateStudyResponse"
        "400": { $ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest" }
        "401": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized" }
    get:
      tags: [studies]
      operationId: listStudies
      summary: List studies (cockpit home)
      description: Read route the cockpit uses to render the study list. Public.
      security: []
      parameters:
        - name: status
          in: query
          required: false
          schema:
            type: string
            enum: [open, done, stopped]
        - name: limit
          in: query
          required: false
          schema: { type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 100, default: 20 }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: A list of studies.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [studies]
                properties:
                  studies:
                    type: array
                    items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Study" }

  /api/studies/{studyId}:
    parameters:
      - $ref: "#/components/parameters/StudyId"
    get:
      tags: [studies]
      operationId: getStudy
      summary: Full study detail / evidence ledger (study detail)
      description: >
        The cockpit's main read and the shape grade_study.py fetches. Returns the
        study plus its dataset version, hypotheses, runs, critiques, decisions,
        feedback, and artifacts — the whole ledger in one call. Public.
      security: []
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The study and its complete ledger.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/StudyDetail"
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }

  /api/profile:
    post:
      tags: [studies]
      operationId: profileDataset
      summary: Profile the dataset (profile_dataset)
      description: >
        Profiles the study's dataset and writes a dataset version: columns with
        dtypes and missingness, candidate leakage columns (flagged, defaulting to
        banned), the split strategy, and the seed.
      security:
        - internalToken: []
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [study_id]
              properties:
                study_id: { type: string }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Dataset profiled; data contract written.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/DatasetVersion"
        "401": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }

  /api/experiments/propose:
    post:
      tags: [experiments]
      operationId: proposeExperiments
      summary: Propose hypothesis cards (propose_experiments)
      description: >
        Returns N hypothesis cards (statement, rationale, model family, candidate
        features, expected outcome). These render as the experiment cards in the
        cockpit; the human approves, edits, or rejects them.
      security:
        - internalToken: []
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [study_id]
              properties:
                study_id: { type: string }
                n:
                  type: integer
                  minimum: 1
                  maximum: 12
                  default: 6
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Proposed hypotheses.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [hypotheses]
                properties:
                  hypotheses:
                    type: array
                    items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Hypothesis" }
        "401": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized" }

  /api/approvals/request:
    post:
      tags: [approvals]
      operationId: requestApproval
      summary: Request human approval (request_approval)
      description: >
        Creates a pending approval the cockpit surfaces (e.g. launching N runs at
        an estimated cost, or unbanning a leakage feature). Compute cannot launch
        until a matching approval is recorded via /api/feedback (type=approval).
      security:
        - internalToken: []
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: "#/components/schemas/ApprovalRequest"
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Pending approval created.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [approval_id, status]
                properties:
                  approval_id: { type: string }
                  status: { type: string, enum: [pending] }
        "401": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized" }

  /api/experiments/launch:
    post:
      tags: [experiments]
      operationId: launchExperiment
      summary: Launch a sandboxed experiment (launch_experiment)
      description: >
        Verifies an approval exists, submits the experiment manifest to the Modal
        runner, and records a run with metrics, params, artifacts, and provenance
        (dataset_hash, code_hash, seed). The manifest is the only thing handed to
        the runner — no arbitrary code. Tuning on 'test' is rejected.
      security:
        - internalToken: []
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [manifest]
              properties:
                manifest: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ExperimentManifest" }
                approval_id:
                  type: string
                  description: The approval authorizing this compute.
            examples:
              baseline:
                $ref: "#/components/examples/LaunchBaseline"
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Run created (may still be running).
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Run" }
        "402":
          description: No approval on file, or budget exceeded.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Error" }
        "401": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized" }
        "422":
          description: Manifest invalid (e.g. banned column in features, tune_on=test).
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Error" }

  /api/runs/query:
    post:
      tags: [experiments]
      operationId: queryRuns
      summary: Query runs (query_runs)
      description: >
        Filter the ledger's runs by metric thresholds, model family, hypothesis,
        tags, or linked critique kind. Powers both the cockpit run table and the
        agent's "show me runs where recall improved but precision dropped" queries.
      security:
        - internalToken: []
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: "#/components/schemas/RunQuery"
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Matching runs.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [runs]
                properties:
                  runs:
                    type: array
                    items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Run" }
        "401": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized" }

  /api/feedback:
    post:
      tags: [feedback]
      operationId: recordHumanFeedback
      summary: Record human feedback (record_human_feedback)
      description: >
        Stores a human judgment and (for natural-language notes) its parsed
        constraints. An approval is feedback of type=approval. The ergonomic
        breakthrough: the human gives judgment, the agent gets a structured
        constraint it can apply to later manifests (applied_feedback_id).
      security:
        - internalToken: []
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: "#/components/schemas/Feedback"
            examples:
              recallOverPrecision:
                $ref: "#/components/examples/FeedbackRecall"
              approval:
                $ref: "#/components/examples/FeedbackApproval"
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Feedback recorded.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Feedback" }
        "401": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized" }

  /api/reports:
    post:
      tags: [reports]
      operationId: writeReport
      summary: Generate the model card (write_report)
      description: >
        Assembles the final report — objective, data, split, experiments table,
        best vs baseline, risks, rejected ideas, next steps, a reproducible
        command, and a provenance footer — stores it in R2, and records an
        artifact of kind=report.
      security:
        - internalToken: []
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [study_id]
              properties:
                study_id: { type: string }
                report_type:
                  type: string
                  enum: [model_card, summary]
                  default: model_card
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Report generated and stored.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Report" }
        "401": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized" }

  /api/grade:
    post:
      tags: [grading]
      operationId: gradeStudy
      summary: Grade against the rubric (grade_study_against_rubric)
      description: >
        Evaluates the study against docs/rubric.json and returns pass/fail per
        check plus an overall verdict. This is the machine-checkable definition of
        done — the Stop hook calls it so "done" is verifiable without a human.
      security:
        - internalToken: []
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [study_id]
              properties:
                study_id: { type: string }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Grading result.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/GradeResult" }
        "401": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }

components:
  securitySchemes:
    internalToken:
      type: http
      scheme: bearer
      description: >
        Shared secret (LABMATE_INTERNAL_TOKEN) between the MCP server and the
        Worker. Not the Cloudflare API token. Generate with `openssl rand -hex 24`.

  parameters:
    StudyId:
      name: studyId
      in: path
      required: true
      schema: { type: string }
      example: study_01HZX

  responses:
    BadRequest:
      description: Malformed request body.
      content:
        application/json:
          schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Error" }
    Unauthorized:
      description: Missing or invalid internal token.
      content:
        application/json:
          schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Error" }
    NotFound:
      description: Resource not found.
      content:
        application/json:
          schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Error" }

  schemas:
    Error:
      type: object
      required: [error]
      properties:
        error: { type: string }
        detail: { type: string }

    Budget:
      type: object
      properties:
        max_trials: { type: integer, default: 20 }
        budget_seconds: { type: integer, default: 600 }

    Study:
      type: object
      required: [id, brief, dataset_id, target, metric]
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        brief: { type: string }
        owner: { type: string }
        task_type:
          type: string
          enum: [binary_classification, regression]
        dataset_id: { type: string }
        target: { type: string }
        metric: { type: string }
        metric_rationale: { type: string }
        budget: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Budget" }
        rubric: { type: string, default: docs/rubric.json }
        status:
          type: string
          enum: [open, done, stopped]
          default: open

    CreateStudyRequest:
      type: object
      required: [brief, dataset_id, target, metric]
      properties:
        brief: { type: string }
        owner: { type: string }
        task_type:
          type: string
          enum: [binary_classification, regression]
        dataset_id: { type: string }
        target: { type: string }
        metric: { type: string }
        metric_rationale: { type: string }
        constraints:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/Constraints"
        budget: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Budget" }
        rubric: { type: string, default: docs/rubric.json }

    CreateStudyResponse:
      type: object
      required: [id]
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        status: { type: string, enum: [open] }

    Constraints:
      type: object
      properties:
        primary_metric: { type: string }
        guardrails:
          type: array
          items:
            type: object
            properties:
              expr: { type: string, examples: ["false_positive_rate <= 0.20"] }
              rationale: { type: string }
        banned_columns:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
        require_interpretability: { type: boolean, default: false }

    ColumnProfile:
      type: object
      required: [name, dtype]
      properties:
        name: { type: string }
        dtype: { type: string }
        missing_fraction: { type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 1 }
        n_unique: { type: integer }
        is_candidate_leakage: { type: boolean, default: false }
        leakage_reason: { type: string }

    SplitStrategy:
      type: object
      required: [strategy, seed]
      properties:
        strategy:
          type: string
          enum: [time_based, stratified]
        time_col: { type: string }
        ratios:
          type: array
          items: { type: number }
          minItems: 3
          maxItems: 3
          description: "[train, validation, test]"
        seed: { type: integer }

    DatasetVersion:
      type: object
      required: [id, study_id, file_hash, row_count]
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        study_id: { type: string }
        file_hash: { type: string }
        row_count: { type: integer }
        columns:
          type: array
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ColumnProfile" }
        target_definition: { type: string }
        split_strategy: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/SplitStrategy" }

    Hypothesis:
      type: object
      required: [id, study_id, statement]
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        study_id: { type: string }
        statement: { type: string, description: "A falsifiable claim." }
        rationale: { type: string }
        model_family: { type: string }
        features:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
        expected_outcome: { type: string }
        status:
          type: string
          enum: [proposed, approved, rejected]

    ModelSpec:
      type: object
      required: [family]
      properties:
        family:
          type: string
          enum:
            - dummy
            - logistic_regression
            - linear_regression
            - random_forest
            - hist_gradient_boosting
            - xgboost
            - lightgbm
        params: { type: object, additionalProperties: true }

    SearchSpec:
      type: object
      properties:
        enabled: { type: boolean, default: false }
        max_trials: { type: integer, minimum: 1, default: 20 }
        timeout_seconds: { type: integer, minimum: 1, default: 600 }
        sampler: { type: string, default: tpe }
        tune_on:
          type: string
          enum: [validation]
          default: validation
          description: Tuning on 'test' is forbidden and rejected by the runner.

    MetricSpec:
      type: object
      required: [primary]
      properties:
        primary:
          type: string
          examples: [recall_at_fpr, pr_auc, roc_auc, rmse, mae]
        max_fpr: { type: number }

    ExperimentManifest:
      type: object
      required: [study_id, dataset_uri, target, task_type, split, features, model, metric]
      properties:
        study_id: { type: string }
        hypothesis_id: { type: string }
        dataset_uri:
          type: string
          description: Where the runner pulls the CSV (R2 key or public URL).
        target: { type: string }
        task_type:
          type: string
          enum: [binary_classification, regression]
        split: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/SplitStrategy" }
        features:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
          description: MUST exclude banned/leaky columns.
        banned_columns:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
        model: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ModelSpec" }
        search: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/SearchSpec" }
        metric: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/MetricSpec" }
        applied_feedback_id:
          type: string
          description: Human feedback id whose parsed constraint shaped this manifest.
        tags:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
          examples: [["baseline"]]

    Run:
      type: object
      required: [id, study_id, hypothesis_id, status]
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        study_id: { type: string }
        hypothesis_id: { type: string }
        manifest_id: { type: string }
        tracker_run_id: { type: string }
        status:
          type: string
          enum: [queued, running, completed, failed]
        metrics: { type: object, additionalProperties: { type: number } }
        params: { type: object, additionalProperties: true }
        artifacts:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: true
          description: name -> { uri, kind }
        rationale: { type: string, description: "What this run tests and why." }
        tags:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
        executor:
          type: string
          const: modal-runner
        dataset_hash: { type: string }
        code_hash: { type: string }
        seed: { type: integer }

    Critique:
      type: object
      required: [id, study_id, kind, finding]
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        study_id: { type: string }
        target_run_id: { type: string }
        kind:
          type: string
          enum: [leakage, test_set_tuning, metric, calibration, robustness]
        finding: { type: string }
        recommendation: { type: string }
        led_to_decision:
          type: string
          enum: [promote, reject, rerun, branch, stop]

    Decision:
      type: object
      required: [id, study_id, action]
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        study_id: { type: string }
        action:
          type: string
          enum: [promote, reject, rerun, branch, stop]
        promoted_run_id: { type: string }
        rejected_run_id: { type: string }
        reason: { type: string }

    Feedback:
      type: object
      required: [study_id, type, content]
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        study_id: { type: string }
        target_id: { type: string }
        type:
          type: string
          enum: [approval, ban_feature, change_metric, increase_budget, focus_segment, note]
        scope: { type: string, enum: [study, hypothesis, run, experiment] }
        content: { type: string }
        parsed_constraints:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: true
          description: "e.g. { primary_metric: 'recall', guardrail: 'false_positive_rate <= 0.20' }"

    ApprovalRequest:
      type: object
      required: [study_id, reason]
      properties:
        study_id: { type: string }
        experiment_ids:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
        reason: { type: string }
        estimated_cost_seconds: { type: integer }

    Artifact:
      type: object
      required: [id, study_id, kind, uri]
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        study_id: { type: string }
        kind: { type: string, enum: [report, plot, model, confusion_matrix] }
        uri: { type: string }
        dataset_hash: { type: string }
        code_hash: { type: string }
        seed: { type: integer }

    Report:
      type: object
      required: [study_id, uri]
      properties:
        study_id: { type: string }
        uri: { type: string, description: R2 location of the rendered report. }
        best_run_id: { type: string }
        baseline_run_id: { type: string }
        compares_best_to_baseline: { type: boolean }
        reproducible_command: { type: string }
        provenance:
          type: object
          properties:
            dataset_hash: { type: string }
            code_hash: { type: string }
            seed: { type: integer }

    RunQuery:
      type: object
      required: [study_id]
      properties:
        study_id: { type: string }
        model_family: { type: string }
        hypothesis_id: { type: string }
        tags:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
        critique_kind:
          type: string
          enum: [leakage, test_set_tuning, metric, calibration, robustness]
        metric_filters:
          type: array
          description: e.g. recall >= 0.7 AND precision < 0.5
          items:
            type: object
            required: [name, op, value]
            properties:
              name: { type: string }
              op: { type: string, enum: ["<", "<=", "=", ">=", ">"] }
              value: { type: number }

    StudyDetail:
      type: object
      required: [study]
      description: The whole evidence ledger in one payload (cockpit + grader read this).
      properties:
        study: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Study" }
        dataset_version: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/DatasetVersion" }
        hypotheses:
          type: array
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Hypothesis" }
        runs:
          type: array
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Run" }
        critiques:
          type: array
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Critique" }
        decisions:
          type: array
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Decision" }
        feedback:
          type: array
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Feedback" }
        artifacts:
          type: array
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Artifact" }
        recommendation:
          type: string
          description: Current agent recommendation rendered in the cockpit.

    GradeResult:
      type: object
      required: [study_id, verdict, checks]
      properties:
        study_id: { type: string }
        rubric_name: { type: string }
        rubric_version: { type: integer }
        verdict:
          type: string
          enum: [done, not_done]
        passed_required: { type: integer }
        total_required: { type: integer }
        checks:
          type: array
          items:
            type: object
            required: [id, required, passed]
            properties:
              id: { type: string }
              category: { type: string }
              required: { type: boolean }
              passed: { type: boolean }
              detail: { type: string }

  examples:
    CreateStudySlaTickets:
      summary: SLA-breach study on the bundled dataset
      value:
        brief: >
          Predict which support tickets will breach SLA. Optimize recall at an
          acceptable false-positive cost. Do not use fields created after ticket
          close.
        owner: team@example.com
        task_type: binary_classification
        dataset_id: sla_tickets
        target: breached_sla
        metric: recall_at_fpr
        metric_rationale: Missed breaches are costlier than false alarms up to 20% FPR.
        constraints:
          primary_metric: recall
          guardrails:
            - expr: "false_positive_rate <= 0.20"

1	# Parallel build plan — front end and back end at the same time
2	
3	The whole point of the OpenAPI spec (`apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml`) is that it
4	lets two tracks move independently. The **contract is the integration point**:
5	the back end implements it; the front end builds against a mock generated from
6	it. You only "integrate" by pointing the cockpit at the real Worker instead of
7	the mock — and if both sides honored the spec, it just works.
8	
9	This plan gives you (1) a git worktree layout so two Claude Code sessions never
10	collide, (2) the exact kickoff prompt and `/goal` for each track, and (3) the
11	rule that keeps them in sync.
12	
13	---
14	
15	## The one rule
16	
17	> **The spec is the source of truth. Code changes to satisfy the spec; the spec
18	> does not drift to match code.** If either track needs the contract changed,
19	> they edit `apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml` on a short-lived `spec/*` branch, both
20	> tracks pull it, then continue. Never let the FE invent a field the spec
21	> doesn't have, and never let the BE return a shape the spec doesn't describe.
22	
23	`npm run spec:lint` (added below) fails CI if the spec is malformed, and the
24	back-end track has a contract test that fails if a response violates the spec.
25	
26	---
27	
28	## 1. Git worktrees
29	
30	Worktrees let one clone have multiple working directories on different branches
31	at once — perfect for running two Claude Code sessions side by side without
32	branch-switching churn or merge stomping.
33	
34	From the repo root (on `main`), create a shared integration branch and two track
35	branches, each in its own directory:
36	
37	```bash
38	# integration branch both tracks merge into
39	git switch -c integration
40	git push -u origin integration
41	
42	# back-end worktree on its own branch
43	git worktree add ../labmate-backend -b track/backend integration
44	
45	# front-end worktree on its own branch
46	git worktree add ../labmate-frontend -b track/frontend integration
47	```
48	
49	You now have three directories sharing one git history:
50	
51	```
52	labmate/            (main / integration — specs, docs, shared packages)
53	labmate-backend/    (track/backend  — apps/web, apps/modal-runner, apps/mcp-server)
54	labmate-frontend/   (track/frontend — apps/web/cockpit or apps/cockpit)
55	```
56	
57	Open a **separate Claude Code session in each track directory**. Each gets its
58	own context, its own `/goal`, and edits its own files. They share the spec via
59	git, not by editing the same files.
60	
61	### Who owns what (avoid write conflicts)
62	
63	| Path | Owner | Notes |
64	|---|---|---|
65	| `apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml` | **shared** | change only via a `spec/*` branch both pull |
66	| `apps/web/src/worker.js` | back end | the control-plane routes |
67	| `apps/web/schema.sql` | back end | D1 tables |
68	| `apps/modal-runner/**` | back end | the fixed runner |
69	| `apps/mcp-server/**` | back end | thin wrappers over the Worker routes |
70	| `packages/schemas/**` | **shared** | change with the spec, in lockstep |
71	| `apps/cockpit/**` (new) | front end | the SPA; talks to the spec, mock first |
72	| `docs/**`, `.claude/**` | shared | coordinate; mostly stable during the build |
73	
74	The front end builds in a **new `apps/cockpit/` directory** rather than editing
75	the Worker's inline `COCKPIT_HTML`, so the two tracks touch disjoint files. The
76	Worker keeps serving a placeholder until you wire the built SPA at the end.
77	
78	### Merging
79	
80	Both tracks merge into `integration` frequently (small, often). Because they
81	edit disjoint paths, merges are clean. Final `integration -> main` once the
82	cockpit points at the real Worker and `npm run guard` is green.
83	
84	```bash
85	# from a track dir, when a slice is done:
86	git add -A && git commit -m "track: <slice>"
87	git switch integration && git merge --no-ff track/backend && git push
88	git switch track/backend   # back to work
89	```
90	
91	---
92	
93	## 2. Generate the mock + types from the spec (do this once, up front)
94	
95	This is what unblocks the front end immediately.
96	
97	```bash
98	# Mock server: serves spec-accurate fake responses on :4010
99	npx @stoplight/prism-cli mock apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml --port 4010
100	
101	# TypeScript types for both tracks, generated from the spec
102	npx openapi-typescript apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml -o packages/api-types/index.ts
103	```
104	
105	Add these to `package.json` so they're one command (the back-end track owns the
106	edit, but both use them):
107	
108	```jsonc
109	"scripts": {
110	  "spec:lint": "npx @redocly/cli lint apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml",
111	  "spec:mock": "npx @stoplight/prism-cli mock apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml --port 4010",
112	  "spec:types": "npx openapi-typescript apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml -o packages/api-types/index.ts",
113	  "spec:docs": "npx @redocly/cli build-docs apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml -o apps/api-spec/index.html"
114	}
115	```
116	
117	The front end sets `VITE_API_BASE=http://localhost:4010` and builds the entire
118	cockpit against the mock. The back end runs `wrangler dev` on :8787 and makes the
119	real routes match the same spec. Flip `VITE_API_BASE` to the wrangler URL to
120	integrate.
121	
122	---
123	
124	## 3. Back-end track — kickoff + goal
125	
126	Open Claude Code in `../labmate-backend`. Paste this brief, then the `/goal`.
127	
128	### Brief (paste first)
129	
130	```
131	You are the BACK-END track for Labmate, an agent-native data science harness.
132	Your contract is apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml — implement the Cloudflare Worker so
133	every route matches it exactly. Read these first:
134	  - apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml   (the contract you must satisfy)
135	  - apps/web/schema.sql          (D1 tables for the evidence ledger)
136	  - packages/schemas/*.schema.json (entity shapes; keep in lockstep with the spec)
137	  - CLAUDE.md                    (hard rules, conventions, provenance)
138	
139	Scope (your files only): apps/web (Worker routes, D1, Durable Object, R2),
140	apps/modal-runner (the fixed runner), apps/mcp-server (thin wrappers over your
141	routes). Do NOT touch apps/cockpit — that's the front-end track.
142	
143	Rules of engagement:
144	  1. The spec is the source of truth. If a route needs a shape the spec lacks,
145	     STOP, propose an edit to apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml, and note it — do not
146	     silently diverge.
147	  2. Every run links to a hypothesis and carries rationale; every critique and
148	     decision is recorded. Provenance (dataset_hash, code_hash, seed) on every
149	     report artifact.
150	  3. Compute launches require a recorded approval; reject launch_experiment with
151	     402 if none exists or budget is exceeded. Reject manifests with banned
152	     columns in features, or tune_on=test, with 422.
153	  4. Tuning happens on validation only. The runner is fixed — no arbitrary code.
154	
155	Write a contract test (tests/contract.api.test.mjs) that boots the Worker with
156	`wrangler dev`, hits each route with the spec's example bodies, and asserts the
157	responses validate against the spec's response schemas. That test is your
158	definition of done for the API surface.
159	```
160	
161	### Goal (paste after)
162	
163	```
164	/goal Implement the Labmate control plane so it satisfies apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml.
165	Done means: apps/web/schema.sql creates tables for study, dataset_version,
166	hypothesis, run, critique, decision, feedback, artifact; every route in the spec
167	is implemented against D1/R2 with bearer-token auth on writes; launch_experiment
168	verifies an approval, submits the manifest to the Modal runner, and records a run
169	with metrics/params/artifacts and provenance; query_runs supports metric, model
170	family, hypothesis, tags, and critique-kind filters; write_report stores a model
171	card in R2 and records a kind=report artifact; grade returns pass/fail per rubric
172	check from docs/rubric.json; and `tests/contract.api.test.mjs` passes against a
173	running `wrangler dev`, with `npm run guard` green.
174	```
175	
176	### Suggested back-end slices (let Claude sequence them)
177	
178	1. `schema.sql` + D1 migration; `GET /api/studies/{id}` returning the empty
179	   ledger shape from the spec. (Unblocks the FE's real-data path early.)
180	2. `POST /api/studies`, `/api/profile`, `/api/experiments/propose`.
181	3. `/api/approvals/request` + `/api/feedback` (incl. the approval gate).
182	4. `/api/experiments/launch` -> Modal runner -> record run + provenance.
183	5. `/api/runs/query` filters; `/api/reports` -> R2; `/api/grade` vs rubric.
184	6. Durable Object event stream (nice-to-have for live cockpit updates).
185	
186	---
187	
188	## 4. Front-end track — kickoff + goal
189	
190	Open Claude Code in `../labmate-frontend`. Paste this brief, then the `/goal`.
191	
192	### Brief (paste first)
193	
194	```
195	You are the FRONT-END track for Labmate, an agent-native data science harness.
196	You build the mission-control cockpit in a NEW directory apps/cockpit (do not
197	edit apps/web — that's the back-end track). Your contract is
198	apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml; build entirely against the Prism mock at
199	http://localhost:4010 using the generated types in packages/api-types.
200	
201	Read first:
202	  - apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml   (every shape you render comes from here)
203	  - docs/BRIEF.md (section 9, the cockpit)  and docs/DEMO_SCRIPT.md
204	  - packages/api-types/index.ts  (generated TS types — import these, do not hand-write shapes)
205	
206	The cockpit is a four-pane mission control, NOT a dashboard:
207	  1. Brief + rubric — objective, metric, guardrails, budget, "done" criteria.
208	  2. Experiment cards — per hypothesis: statement, expected impact, cost,
209	     status, latest metric, agent rationale, and approve / deny / rerun buttons.
210	  3. Evidence ledger — timeline of runs, notes, critiques, human feedback.
211	  4. Current recommendation — e.g. "Promote model 7 after a calibration check."
212	Plus a natural-language feedback box that POSTs to /api/feedback, and a
213	"Generate report" button that POSTs to /api/reports and links the artifact.
214	
215	Rules of engagement:
216	  1. The spec is the source of truth. If you need a field it lacks, STOP and
217	     propose a spec edit — do not invent response shapes or hardcode mock data
218	     beyond what the spec describes.
219	  2. Read everything from GET /api/studies and GET /api/studies/{id}. All writes
220	     go to the documented POST routes with the bearer token from an env var.
221	  3. Make it resilient: loading and empty states for every pane, optimistic UI
222	     on approve/deny, and graceful handling of a run still "running".
223	  4. Use VITE_API_BASE so flipping from the mock (:4010) to the real Worker
224	     (:8787 / the deployed URL) is a one-line change.
225	```
226	
227	### Goal (paste after)
228	
229	```
230	/goal Build the Labmate cockpit in apps/cockpit against the Prism mock at
231	VITE_API_BASE. Done means: a study-list view (GET /api/studies) and a study
232	detail view rendering all four panes from GET /api/studies/{studyId}; experiment
233	cards with working approve/deny/rerun that POST to /api/feedback and
234	/api/approvals/request; a natural-language feedback box; a run table fed by the
235	study detail's runs with status, metrics, and linked critiques; a "Generate
236	report" button hitting /api/reports that surfaces the artifact link; every pane
237	has loading and empty states; the app imports types from packages/api-types and
238	builds with `npm run build` clean; and switching VITE_API_BASE to the wrangler
239	URL renders real data with no code change.
240	```
241	
242	### Suggested front-end slices
243	
244	1. Vite + TS app skeleton in `apps/cockpit`; API client wrapper around
245	   `VITE_API_BASE` that injects the bearer token; import `packages/api-types`.
246	2. Study-list + study-detail shell with the four empty panes (loading/empty
247	   states first — they're most of the resilience).
248	3. Experiment cards from `hypotheses` + latest run metric; approve/deny/rerun.
249	4. Evidence ledger timeline merging runs + critiques + feedback by time.
250	5. Feedback box -> `/api/feedback`; recommendation pane; report button.
251	6. Polish pass: optimistic updates, "running" spinners, error toasts.
252	
253	---
254	
255	## 5. Integration (the easy part, if you held the contract)
256	
257	```bash
258	# 1. Back end is deployed or running:  wrangler dev  (:8787)
259	# 2. Point the cockpit at it:
260	echo "VITE_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:8787" > apps/cockpit/.env.local
261	# 3. Run the back end's contract test against the same URL:
262	npm run --workspace=apps/web test:contract
263	# 4. Click through the demo in docs/DEMO_SCRIPT.md end to end.
264	```
265	
266	If a pane renders wrong, the response didn't match the spec → fix the **back
267	end** (or, if the spec was wrong, fix the spec and regenerate types). The FE
268	should not be patched to accommodate an off-spec response.
269	
270	Finally, build the cockpit and have the Worker serve it (replace the inline
271	`COCKPIT_HTML` with the built `apps/cockpit/dist`), then merge `integration` to
272	`main`, deploy, and confirm `LABMATE_PUBLIC_URL` serves the real cockpit.
273	
274	---
275	
276	## 6. Driving both with one orchestration story (for judging)
277	
278	The Orchestration criterion rewards a setup another team could rerun. Yours is:
279	
280	- **One contract** (`openapi.yaml`) both tracks build against.
281	- **Two `/goal`s**, each with a machine-checkable done: the BE's
282	  `contract.api.test.mjs` and the FE's `npm run build` + mock-to-real swap.
283	- **`npm run guard`** (schema-check + lint + tests) plus **`npm run spec:lint`**
284	  gate every merge in CI.
285	- The **self-correction moment** still lives in the back-end + workflow track
286	  (the critic catching the planted leakage / test-set tuning).
287	
288	Show the judges: the spec, the two goals, the two green "done" signals, and the
289	moment a track caught a contract mismatch (or the agent caught the leakage) and
290	fixed it without you.
291	
292	---
293	
294	## Quick reference
295	
296	```bash
297	# worktrees
298	git worktree add ../labmate-backend  -b track/backend  integration
299	git worktree add ../labmate-frontend -b track/frontend integration
300	git worktree list
301	git worktree remove ../labmate-frontend   # when done
302	
303	# spec tooling
304	npm run spec:lint     # validate the contract
305	npm run spec:mock     # mock server on :4010 (front end builds against this)
306	npm run spec:types    # regenerate packages/api-types from the spec
307	npm run spec:docs     # human-readable API docs
308	
309	# keep in sync
310	git switch integration && git pull        # both tracks, often
311	```

| `apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml` | **shared** | change only via a `spec/*` branch both pull |
| `apps/web/src/worker.js` | back end | the control-plane routes |
| `apps/web/schema.sql` | back end | D1 tables |
| `apps/modal-runner/**` | back end | the fixed runner |
| `apps/mcp-server/**` | back end | thin wrappers over the Worker routes |
| `packages/schemas/**` | **shared** | change with the spec, in lockstep |
| `apps/cockpit/**` (new) | front end | the SPA; talks to the spec, mock first |
| `docs/**`, `.claude/**` | shared | coordinate; mostly stable during the build |

The front end builds in a **new `apps/cockpit/` directory** rather than editing
the Worker's inline `COCKPIT_HTML`, so the two tracks touch disjoint files. The
Worker keeps serving a placeholder until you wire the built SPA at the end.

### Merging

Both tracks merge into `integration` frequently (small, often). Because they
edit disjoint paths, merges are clean. Final `integration -> main` once the
cockpit points at the real Worker and `npm run guard` is green.

```bash
# from a track dir, when a slice is done:
git add -A && git commit -m "track: <slice>"
git switch integration && git merge --no-ff track/backend && git push
git switch track/backend   # back to work
```

---

## 2. Generate the mock + types from the spec (do this once, up front)

This is what unblocks the front end immediately.

```bash
# Mock server: serves spec-accurate fake responses on :4010
npx @stoplight/prism-cli mock apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml --port 4010

# TypeScript types for both tracks, generated from the spec
npx openapi-typescript apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml -o packages/api-types/index.ts
```

Add these to `package.json` so they're one command (the back-end track owns the
edit, but both use them):

```jsonc
"scripts": {
  "spec:lint": "npx @redocly/cli lint apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml",
  "spec:mock": "npx @stoplight/prism-cli mock apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml --port 4010",
  "spec:types": "npx openapi-typescript apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml -o packages/api-types/index.ts",
  "spec:docs": "npx @redocly/cli build-docs apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml -o apps/api-spec/index.html"
}
```

The front end sets `VITE_API_BASE=http://localhost:4010` and builds the entire
cockpit against the mock. The back end runs `wrangler dev` on :8787 and makes the
real routes match the same spec. Flip `VITE_API_BASE` to the wrangler URL to
integrate.

---

## 3. Back-end track — kickoff + goal

Open Claude Code in `../labmate-backend`. Paste this brief, then the `/goal`.

### Brief (paste first)

```
You are the BACK-END track for Labmate, an agent-native data science harness.
Your contract is apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml — implement the Cloudflare Worker so
every route matches it exactly. Read these first:
  - apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml   (the contract you must satisfy)
  - apps/web/schema.sql          (D1 tables for the evidence ledger)
  - packages/schemas/*.schema.json (entity shapes; keep in lockstep with the spec)
  - CLAUDE.md                    (hard rules, conventions, provenance)

Scope (your files only): apps/web (Worker routes, D1, Durable Object, R2),
apps/modal-runner (the fixed runner), apps/mcp-server (thin wrappers over your
routes). Do NOT touch apps/cockpit — that's the front-end track.

Rules of engagement:
  1. The spec is the source of truth. If a route needs a shape the spec lacks,
     STOP, propose an edit to apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml, and note it — do not
     silently diverge.
  2. Every run links to a hypothesis and carries rationale; every critique and
     decision is recorded. Provenance (dataset_hash, code_hash, seed) on every
     report artifact.
  3. Compute launches require a recorded approval; reject launch_experiment with
     402 if none exists or budget is exceeded. Reject manifests with banned
     columns in features, or tune_on=test, with 422.
  4. Tuning happens on validation only. The runner is fixed — no arbitrary code.

Write a contract test (tests/contract.api.test.mjs) that boots the Worker with
`wrangler dev`, hits each route with the spec's example bodies, and asserts the
responses validate against the spec's response schemas. That test is your
definition of done for the API surface.
```

### Goal (paste after)

```
/goal Implement the Labmate control plane so it satisfies apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml.
Done means: apps/web/schema.sql creates tables for study, dataset_version,
hypothesis, run, critique, decision, feedback, artifact; every route in the spec
is implemented against D1/R2 with bearer-token auth on writes; launch_experiment
verifies an approval, submits the manifest to the Modal runner, and records a run
with metrics/params/artifacts and provenance; query_runs supports metric, model
family, hypothesis, tags, and critique-kind filters; write_report stores a model
card in R2 and records a kind=report artifact; grade returns pass/fail per rubric
check from docs/rubric.json; and `tests/contract.api.test.mjs` passes against a
running `wrangler dev`, with `npm run guard` green.
```

### Suggested back-end slices (let Claude sequence them)

1. `schema.sql` + D1 migration; `GET /api/studies/{id}` returning the empty
   ledger shape from the spec. (Unblocks the FE's real-data path early.)
2. `POST /api/studies`, `/api/profile`, `/api/experiments/propose`.
3. `/api/approvals/request` + `/api/feedback` (incl. the approval gate).
4. `/api/experiments/launch` -> Modal runner -> record run + provenance.
5. `/api/runs/query` filters; `/api/reports` -> R2; `/api/grade` vs rubric.
6. Durable Object event stream (nice-to-have for live cockpit updates).

---

## 4. Front-end track — kickoff + goal

Open Claude Code in `../labmate-frontend`. Paste this brief, then the `/goal`.

### Brief (paste first)

```
You are the FRONT-END track for Labmate, an agent-native data science harness.
You build the mission-control cockpit in a NEW directory apps/cockpit (do not
edit apps/web — that's the back-end track). Your contract is
apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml; build entirely against the Prism mock at
http://localhost:4010 using the generated types in packages/api-types.

Read first:
  - apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml   (every shape you render comes from here)
  - docs/BRIEF.md (section 9, the cockpit)  and docs/DEMO_SCRIPT.md
  - packages/api-types/index.ts  (generated TS types — import these, do not hand-write shapes)

The cockpit is a four-pane mission control, NOT a dashboard:
  1. Brief + rubric — objective, metric, guardrails, budget, "done" criteria.
  2. Experiment cards — per hypothesis: statement, expected impact, cost,
     status, latest metric, agent rationale, and approve / deny / rerun buttons.
  3. Evidence ledger — timeline of runs, notes, critiques, human feedback.
  4. Current recommendation — e.g. "Promote model 7 after a calibration check."
Plus a natural-language feedback box that POSTs to /api/feedback, and a
"Generate report" button that POSTs to /api/reports and links the artifact.

Rules of engagement:
  1. The spec is the source of truth. If you need a field it lacks, STOP and
     propose a spec edit — do not invent response shapes or hardcode mock data
     beyond what the spec describes.
  2. Read everything from GET /api/studies and GET /api/studies/{id}. All writes
     go to the documented POST routes with the bearer token from an env var.
  3. Make it resilient: loading and empty states for every pane, optimistic UI
     on approve/deny, and graceful handling of a run still "running".
  4. Use VITE_API_BASE so flipping from the mock (:4010) to the real Worker
     (:8787 / the deployed URL) is a one-line change.
```

### Goal (paste after)

```
/goal Build the Labmate cockpit in apps/cockpit against the Prism mock at
VITE_API_BASE. Done means: a study-list view (GET /api/studies) and a study
detail view rendering all four panes from GET /api/studies/{studyId}; experiment
cards with working approve/deny/rerun that POST to /api/feedback and
/api/approvals/request; a natural-language feedback box; a run table fed by the
study detail's runs with status, metrics, and linked critiques; a "Generate
report" button hitting /api/reports that surfaces the artifact link; every pane
has loading and empty states; the app imports types from packages/api-types and
builds with `npm run build` clean; and switching VITE_API_BASE to the wrangler
URL renders real data with no code change.
```

### Suggested front-end slices

1. Vite + TS app skeleton in `apps/cockpit`; API client wrapper around
   `VITE_API_BASE` that injects the bearer token; import `packages/api-types`.
2. Study-list + study-detail shell with the four empty panes (loading/empty
   states first — they're most of the resilience).
3. Experiment cards from `hypotheses` + latest run metric; approve/deny/rerun.
4. Evidence ledger timeline merging runs + critiques + feedback by time.
5. Feedback box -> `/api/feedback`; recommendation pane; report button.
6. Polish pass: optimistic updates, "running" spinners, error toasts.

---

## 5. Integration (the easy part, if you held the contract)

```bash
# 1. Back end is deployed or running:  wrangler dev  (:8787)
# 2. Point the cockpit at it:
echo "VITE_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:8787" > apps/cockpit/.env.local
# 3. Run the back end's contract test against the same URL:
npm run --workspace=apps/web test:contract
# 4. Click through the demo in docs/DEMO_SCRIPT.md end to end.
```

If a pane renders wrong, the response didn't match the spec → fix the **back
end** (or, if the spec was wrong, fix the spec and regenerate types). The FE
should not be patched to accommodate an off-spec response.

Finally, build the cockpit and have the Worker serve it (replace the inline
`COCKPIT_HTML` with the built `apps/cockpit/dist`), then merge `integration` to
`main`, deploy, and confirm `LABMATE_PUBLIC_URL` serves the real cockpit.

---

## 6. Driving both with one orchestration story (for judging)

The Orchestration criterion rewards a setup another team could rerun. Yours is:

- **One contract** (`openapi.yaml`) both tracks build against.
- **Two `/goal`s**, each with a machine-checkable done: the BE's
  `contract.api.test.mjs` and the FE's `npm run build` + mock-to-real swap.
- **`npm run guard`** (schema-check + lint + tests) plus **`npm run spec:lint`**
  gate every merge in CI.
- The **self-correction moment** still lives in the back-end + workflow track
  (the critic catching the planted leakage / test-set tuning).

Show the judges: the spec, the two goals, the two green "done" signals, and the
moment a track caught a contract mismatch (or the agent caught the leakage) and
fixed it without you.

---

## Quick reference

```bash
# worktrees
git worktree add ../labmate-backend  -b track/backend  integration
git worktree add ../labmate-frontend -b track/frontend integration
git worktree list
git worktree remove ../labmate-frontend   # when done

# spec tooling
npm run spec:lint     # validate the contract
npm run spec:mock     # mock server on :4010 (front end builds against this)
npm run spec:types    # regenerate packages/api-types from the spec
npm run spec:docs     # human-readable API docs

# keep in sync
git switch integration && git pull        # both tracks, often
```

# Environment & keys

Copy `.env.example` → `.env` and fill these in. `./scripts/preflight.sh` validates them.

## Anthropic
- **ANTHROPIC_API_KEY** — from https://console.anthropic.com/settings/keys. At Build Day
  you'll get a $500 credits link (24h expiry) handed out on the day; redeem it and use that
  key. Ask in `#credit-questions` on Discord if you don't have it.
- **ANTHROPIC_MODEL** — leave as `claude-opus-4-8`. Judges weight creative Opus 4.8 use, so
  keep the headline reasoning calls (planning, leakage review, critique, feedback parsing)
  on Opus.

## Modal (experiment execution)
1. Create an account at https://modal.com.
2. `pip install modal` then `modal token new` — this writes `~/.modal.toml` and prints a
   token id + secret. Put them in **MODAL_TOKEN_ID** / **MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET**.
3. Deploy the runner: `modal deploy apps/modal-runner/runner.py`. Modal prints a web URL
   for the FastAPI endpoint — paste it into **MODAL_RUNNER_URL**.

## Cloudflare (cockpit + control plane)
1. **CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID** — dash.cloudflare.com, right sidebar.
2. **CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN** — create a token with edit perms for Workers, D1, R2, and
   Durable Objects.
3. `npx wrangler d1 create labmate` → paste the printed `database_id` into
   **CLOUDFLARE_D1_DATABASE_ID** (and into `apps/web/wrangler.toml`).
4. `npx wrangler r2 bucket create labmate-artifacts` → **CLOUDFLARE_R2_BUCKET**.
5. After `npx wrangler deploy`, your Worker URL becomes **LABMATE_PUBLIC_URL** (your
   submission's live URL).

## MCP server (local)
- **MCP_SERVER_PORT** — default `8787`.
- **LABMATE_INTERNAL_TOKEN** — shared secret between MCP server and Worker. Generate with
  `openssl rand -hex 24`.

## Optional guardrails
- **LABMATE_DEFAULT_MAX_TRIALS** (default 20) and **LABMATE_DEFAULT_BUDGET_SECONDS**
  (default 600) cap Optuna/compute unless the human raises them in the cockpit.

## Security notes
- `.env` is gitignored — never commit it. The repo must be public for judging, so keep all
  secrets out of it.
- The Modal runner has no arbitrary network egress; the MCP server talks to Cloudflare with
  `LABMATE_INTERNAL_TOKEN`, not your Cloudflare API token.

# Labmate API & cockpit — what we're building

This README explains the thing the OpenAPI spec describes and why it's shaped the
way it is, so the front-end and back-end tracks share one mental model. For the
parallel-work mechanics (worktrees, prompts, goals), see
[`docs/PARALLEL_BUILD.md`](../../docs/PARALLEL_BUILD.md). For the product framing,
see [`docs/BRIEF.md`](../../docs/BRIEF.md).

---

## The product in one paragraph

Labmate is an **agent-native data science harness**. A human gives a brief, a
dataset, a target, a metric, and constraints. Claude profiles the data, proposes
hypotheses, runs controlled experiments in a sandbox, critiques its own results,
folds in human feedback, and produces a reproducible report. Everything the agent
believes, does, and is corrected on is captured in an **evidence ledger**:
*hypothesis → experiment → evidence → decision*. The ledger is the product; the
cockpit is how a human steers it.

---

## What the API is
